svg.title: Pion exchange between nucleons, at the quark level
svg.desc: A quark-level Feynman diagram of the interaction in which a proton and a neutron exchange a π⁺. A d–anti-d pair is created near the proton (d, u, u). One of the proton’s up quarks leaves with the anti-down quark as a π⁺, and the new down quark stays behind, so the proton becomes a neutron (d, u, d). At the neutron (d, d, u), the anti-down quark annihilates with a down quark and the up quark stays, so the neutron becomes a proton (u, d, u). Wavy lines are gluons exchanged among the quarks.
